The pattern behind the busy weeks

Thousands of years ago, Babylonian astronomers wrote down every eclipse, night after night, until a pattern appeared. Today we call it the saros. With it, they could see what was coming decades ahead.

Your L&D team already sees signals like these every week. Most of them are lost in email and spreadsheets:

01

The request that keeps coming back.

Three regions ask for the same refresher. It points to a gap nobody has named yet.

02

The project that always waits in the same place.

Approvals stall at the same step, quarter after quarter.

03

The skill nobody trained for.

A new system goes live; the onboarding path stays the same.

04

The report that counts completions.

Leadership asks what changed, and the data to answer was never recorded.

Saros is built to record those signals, so they become a pattern you can act on.

7 stages, 5 portals

How the Saros learning operations platform works: seven stages, five portals

Each stage happens in the portal of the person who owns it, and the KPI defined in the request follows the project all the way to the results report.

01 / 07 Saros

Prediction

Saros reads the patterns in past requests, projects and results, and predicts which training the company will need before anyone asks.

Business requesterL&D teamContent studioInstructorLearner
Sample record REQ-0418Prediction
KPITime to productivitybaseline recorded
  1. Prediction. Saros reads the patterns in past requests, projects and results, and predicts which training the company will need before anyone asks. (Saros)
  2. Assessment. The business area confirms the need in a four-step form, and L&D assesses it: whether training is the answer, plus scope, format and effort. (L&D team)
  3. Design. The content studio designs the solution on one of 12 instructional architectures: objectives, structure and formats. (Content studio)
  4. Development. The content studio builds the pieces with versions and a schedule, and the business area approves them before they go to the LMS. (Content studio)
  5. Engagement. Instructors run in-person, Microsoft Teams or self-paced sessions and keep learners engaged, with attendance and grades. (Instructor)
  6. Learning. Learners follow their agenda and paths on any device. (Learner)
  7. Results. L&D reports the pilot, adjustments and rollout against the original KPI. (L&D team)

Training request intake software that starts every project with a KPI

Saros training request intake software replaces the email, the chat message and the hallway conversation with one guided form. Every request arrives with the business problem, the audience and the KPI it should move, so L&D can triage, score and decide before anyone builds a course.

Try it with a real request Watch the 90-second tour
Processes and tasks5 tasks · 7 skills
KPIs3 KPIs complete
Trainings5 trainings
Users80 people

Why most training requests arrive incomplete

Most requests describe a solution (“we need a course on X”) instead of a problem. Without the business goal, the audience and a way to measure success, L&D has two bad options: build what was asked and hope it works, or spend days in meetings reconstructing the request.

%

It is the most common pain in the function. Prioritizing multiple demands is the number one challenge for talent development teams, cited by 46% in the ATD 2026 State of the Industry report.

How training request intake software works in Saros

Intake in Saros is a short, standard L&D intake process that every business area follows, with L&D in control of what happens next.

  1. 01

    The requester describes the problem

    A four-step form asks for the challenge, the behaviors that should change, the audience (roles, regions, languages) and the business KPI with its current baseline. The requester gets a ticket number and can follow the status.

  2. 02

    L&D triages the request

    L&D checks whether training is the right answer or whether the cause is a process, a tool or an incentive. Requests that need something other than a course get a recommendation instead of a project.

  3. 03

    L&D scores and decides

    Each request is scored on business impact, audience size, risk, readiness and effort. The score and the reason are shared with the requester, and approved requests enter the project pipeline with the KPI attached.

Training request intake software: frequently asked questions

Bring your own questions.

To a 30-minute walkthrough, with the product open.

Book a 30-minute walkthrough

Software that standardizes how business areas ask L&D for training. Instead of emails and ad hoc meetings, requesters fill in a guided form, and L&D triages, prioritizes and tracks each request in one place.

No. You pay for the platform, not per user, so managers outside L&D can submit requests through the Business Requester portal at no extra cost.

Yes. The intake is yours to shape. Add, remove or reword questions so the form speaks your company’s language and asks for what your L&D team needs to decide. Requesters see a form that feels made for them, and your team gets requests that arrive ready to triage.

They stay on record with the decision and the reason, so you can see demand patterns over time and explain choices to stakeholders.

A form tool collects answers; Saros connects the request to triage, scoring, the project pipeline and the results report, so the KPI follows the work from start to finish. Saros also recommends the format. Its format recommendation engine weighs the audience, the goal and the context of each request, and points to the best fit before production starts: a one-pager, microlearning, a live session or a full course. Fewer courses built by default, more solutions that fit the problem.

How healthy is the way your team operates?

The L&D Operating Health Check is a free, 7-minute L&D maturity assessment. Answer 30 questions about how work really moves through your learning function and get a Health Score from 0 to 100, your operating profile, an estimate of the hours your team loses to coordination and recommendations for your biggest opportunity. You see your score without giving an email.

ReactiveDevelopingHealthyHigh-Performance

The five dimensions we measure

  1. 01

    Strategic alignment

    how L&D priorities are set and how visible they are to the business.

  2. 02

    Demand and prioritization

    how requests arrive, are assessed and are prioritized.

  3. 03

    Workflow and production

    how defined and visible the path from request to launch is.

  4. 04

    Capacity and collaboration

    how well you see workload across people, teams, SMEs and vendors.

  5. 05

    Data, AI and impact

    how you use operational data and AI, and what you measure beyond completion.

How the L&D maturity assessment is scored

You answer 20 questions on a 1-to-5 scale, four per dimension, plus six about your organization and four about your operation in numbers. Each dimension score is the average of its four answers, converted to 0–100; the Health Score is the average of the five dimensions. The coordination estimate multiplies your L&D headcount by 1,760 working hours a year, your share of time on coordination and a $60 loaded hourly cost.

Your answers may be included, anonymized and aggregated, in Saros research such as the State of Learning Operations report. We never publish names, emails or company names.

Home/The Saros platform/Project pipeline

L&D project management software built around how training gets made

Every training project in one pipeline, from the approved request to the results report. See the stage, the owner, the deadline and how many days each project has been waiting, before a launch date slips.

See your coordination cost in 1 minute Watch the 90-second tour

Why generic tools fall short as L&D project management software

Generic project tools track tasks. Training projects have a shape of their own: a business owner who must approve content, subject matter experts with little time, versions of the same course, classes to schedule and a KPI to report at the end. When that lives in a task board plus a spreadsheet plus email, nobody can say which projects are late and why without asking around.

%

42% of training and development teams name reducing manual processes as a top priority, according to Tovuti’s 2025 State of the Industry survey. A pipeline replaces status emails and spreadsheets with one shared view.

01Status meetings exist because the status is not visible anywhere.
02Approvals wait in inboxes, and nobody sees how long.
03The KPI from the original request is lost by the time the course launches.

If this sounds familiar, the coordination cost calculator → estimates what it costs your team in hours and dollars.

How the Saros pipeline works

The pipeline follows the seven stages of a training project: prediction, assessment, design, development, engagement, learning and results. Every project carries its owner, deadline and the KPI it came in with.

  1. 01

    Projects arrive ready to plan

    Approved requests from guided training intake → enter the backlog with the business problem, audience and KPI already filled in. Assessment adds scope, format and effort.

  2. 02

    Days in stage, not just due dates

    Each card shows how long the project has been in its current stage. A project that has spent 26 days in diagnosis stands out before it becomes a missed launch.

  3. 03

    Approvals inside the workflow

    The business area approves content in its own portal before anything is published to the LMS. Every version is kept, so you know which one was approved and by whom.

  4. 04

    Bottleneck review by stage

    Filter by stage, owner, business area or region to see where work piles up. Use it in the weekly meeting instead of a status round.

  5. 05

    Your current backlog on day one

    Projects in progress are imported from your spreadsheets or project tools, with stage, owner and due date, so the pipeline reflects reality from the start.

AI course creation grounded in instructional design

Choose the content architecture before AI writes a word. Saros drafts one-pagers, guides, manuals, infographics and SCORM 1.2 packages on one of 12 instructional architectures, in your company’s design system. Your designers review and approve every piece.

Why generic AI content misses the learning objective

General-purpose AI writes fast. It does not know who the audience is, what they should do differently on the job or which KPI the business asked for. The result reads well and teaches little, and your designers spend the time they saved fixing structure.

Most instructional designers already use AI (80%, according to ATD’s 2025 research), and many say it has cut course design time. Far fewer can say what it changed for the business: only 37% of HR managers measure training success by business impact (TalentLMS 2026). Saros starts from the other end: the objective and the model come first.

Home/The Saros platform/Role-based learning paths

Role-based learning paths built from real tasks and skills

Pick a channel, a role and a function. Saros crosses the tasks, skills and training history of that role to build onboarding and refresher paths, and delivers them in waves so people learn what they need when they need it.

Find your L&D operating profile (7 minutes) Watch the 90-second tour

Why one-size-fits-all curricula waste time

A store manager and a contact center agent should not start with the same course list. When paths are built by hand in a spreadsheet, they drift out of date the moment a role changes, and new hires sit through content that does not match their job.

01Paths are copied from the last cohort instead of built from the role.
02Skills with no training behind them go unnoticed.
03Nobody can say which path a person is on, or how far along they are.

Learning hours per employee rose from 13.7 in 2024 to 16.7 in 2025 (ATD 2026 State of the Industry). Paths built from the role make those hours count.

How Saros builds role-based learning paths

  1. 01

    Your job architecture, once

    Import roles, functions, tasks and skills one time. That becomes the map every path is built on.

  2. 02

    AI proposes the path

    Choose a channel (for example stores, contact center or field sales), a role and a function. The AI crosses the role’s tasks and skills with your existing content and training history, and proposes an onboarding or refresher path. Your team edits and approves it.

  3. 03

    Delivered in waves

    Paths are released in waves, so new hires get the essentials in the first days and the rest when it becomes useful on the job.

  4. 04

    Gaps become projects

    When a skill has no content behind it, Saros flags it. One click turns the gap into a content project in the pipeline.

Why completion rates do not convince leadership

%

Completions show that people finished a course. They do not show that sales went up, errors went down or new hires got productive faster. Only 37% of HR managers measure training success by business impact (TalentLMS 2026), and most of the time the reason is practical: the KPI and its baseline were never recorded when the request came in.

Saros fixes the start of the chain, so the end can be reported.

StartThe request records the KPI and its baseline
EndThe results report shows impact against that KPI

How Saros learning analytics link classes to KPIs

  1. 01

    The KPI is captured at intake

    Every request arrives with the business KPI, its current value and the target. Requests without a KPI do not reach the backlog. Training intake →

    Results follow the same project

    The project carries that KPI through production, classes and learning. Attendance, grades and path progress are recorded along the way.

  3. 03

    Compare the pilot with the baseline

    The results stage shows the pilot cohort against the baseline and the target, then the rollout. Filter by cohort, channel, region or format.

  4. 04

    Operational metrics too

    The same dashboard shows how L&D runs: request-to-launch cycle time, days in each stage, projects per owner and adoption by business area.

CLO software: run L&D like an operation the business can see

Every change in a company passes through L&D first. Saros gives you the record to prove it: every initiative tied to a business goal, the whole portfolio in one view and impact reported against the KPI the business asked for.

What CLOs are asked to prove

$

Learning hours per employee went up from 13.7 to 16.7 in 2025, while direct spend per employee fell from $1,254 to $846 (ATD 2026 State of the Industry). You are delivering more with less, and the board still asks the same question: what did it change?

Three things make that question hard to answer:

01Requests arrive without a goal, so there is nothing to measure against.
02The portfolio lives in several tools, so trade-offs are invisible to stakeholders.
03Reports show completions, because that is the data that exists.

How CLO software connects the portfolio to business goals

  1. 01

    Every request starts with a goal

    Guided intake asks for the business problem, the audience and the KPI with its baseline. Requests without a KPI do not reach the backlog. Training intake →

  2. 02

    The portfolio in one view

    See every initiative by business area, stage, owner and goal. When an urgent request arrives, you can show what it would displace.

  3. 03

    Impact against the KPI

    Pilot results are compared with the baseline and reported by cohort, channel and region. KPI in, KPI out. Learning analytics →

  4. 04

    Operational health of your function

    Cycle time from request to launch, days in each stage and capacity by team give you the numbers to defend headcount and priorities.

L&D ROI for CFOs: see where the budget goes and what it returned

US organizations spent $102.8 billion on training in 2025. Most finance teams can see the invoices, not the return. Saros records the business KPI, its baseline and the cost of every training project, so L&D spend can be reviewed like any other investment.

Put a dollar figure on coordination (1 minute) See a sample CFO report

Why L&D spend is hard to evaluate today

The number comes from Training Magazine’s 2025 Training Industry Report. The difficulty comes from how the work is recorded:

01

No baseline

Training requests rarely state the metric they should move, or its current value.

02

Hidden costs

Vendor invoices are visible; the hours your L&D team spends coordinating, chasing approvals and rebuilding requests are not.

03

Completions instead of results

Only 37% of HR managers measure training success by business impact (TalentLMS 2026).

How Saros makes L&D ROI measurable

  1. 01

    A baseline before the money is spent

    Every request records the business KPI, its current value and the target before it becomes a project. Training intake →

  2. 02

    Cost and effort per project

    Assessment records scope, format and effort. The pipeline shows how long each project took and where it waited. [confirmar: a Saros registra custo por projeto (horas internas e fornecedores)?]

  3. 03

    Results against the baseline

    Pilot results are compared with the baseline by cohort, channel and region, before a full rollout is funded. Learning analytics →

  4. 04

    The cost of coordination, in dollars

    The coordination cost calculator → estimates what your L&D team’s coordination work costs per year (headcount × 1,760 hours × share of time on coordination × hourly cost), and produces a one-page report you can review with your L&D leader.

Skills-based learning for HR: connect roles, skills and the people who need them

HR owns the job architecture. L&D owns the courses. Saros connects the two, so every role has a learning path built from its real tasks and skills, and every skill without training shows up before it becomes a performance problem.

Find your L&D operating profile (7 minutes) Watch the 90-second tour

Where learning and HR data disconnect

01Roles change faster than curriculaA new process or system changes the job; the onboarding list stays the same.
02Skills live in one system, courses in anotherNobody can say which skills have no training behind them.
03Access is all or nothingRegional managers either see everyone’s data or nothing useful.
04Onboarding is measured by completion, not by time to productivity in the role.

How Saros delivers skills-based learning for HR

  1. 01

    Your job architecture as the map

    Import roles, functions, tasks and skills once. Every learning path is built on that map.

  2. 02

    Paths by role, in waves

    AI crosses each role’s tasks and skills with your content and training history to propose onboarding and refresher paths, delivered in waves. L&D reviews and approves. Role-based learning paths →

  3. 03

    Skill gaps become projects

    Skills with no training behind them are flagged and can become content projects in one click.

  4. 04

    Access by region, channel and hierarchy

    Managers see their own people. Learners see their own agenda and path. Each role works in its own portal. Role portals →

Frontline training operations across regions, channels and shifts

Stores, contact centers, field sales and service teams learn on the floor, on different shifts and in different places. Saros runs it from one system: paths by role, classes with attendance, mobile access and results by region and channel.

Find your L&D operating profile (7 minutes) Watch the 90-second tour

Why frontline training is hard to run at scale

01Turnover keeps onboarding running all yearEvery week brings a new cohort, in a different region.
02People are not at a deskTraining has to fit a shift and work on a phone.
03Instructors are spread outRosters, attendance and grades end up in local spreadsheets.
04Every region adapts the contentNobody is sure which version is current.
05Results are reported by headcount trained, not by the store or queue metric the business cares about.

How Saros runs frontline training

  1. 01

    Paths by channel and role

    Pick a channel (stores, contact center, field), a role and a function. Saros builds onboarding and refresher paths from the role’s tasks and skills, and delivers them in waves. Role-based learning paths →

  2. 02

    On the floor, on any device

    The Learner portal shows each person their agenda, activities and path on a phone or tablet, with XP, levels and campaigns such as a safety week. Role portals →

  3. 03

    Classes with attendance, wherever they happen

    Instructors run in-person, Microsoft Teams or self-paced sessions and record attendance and grades in the Instructor portal.

  4. 04

    One version of the content

    Every piece is versioned and approved before it is published, so every region uses the current one.

  5. 05

    Results by region and channel

    Compare cohorts by store, region or queue against the KPI from the request, such as time to productivity or first-contact resolution.

About Saros by ReFrame

Every change in a company passes through L&D first. Before a product is launched, someone learns to sell it. Before a team grows, someone learns to lead it. We built Saros so L&D can show the business what learning makes possible.

Our storyThe teamThe methodContact

Why ReFrame built Saros

A name borrowed from the oldest pattern-reading in history, and a platform built for the people who see the business change first.

  1. The pattern

    They paid attention

    Thousands of years ago, Babylonian astronomers recorded every eclipse, night after night, until a pattern appeared. Today we call it the saros. With it, they could see what was coming decades in advance. They did not guess. They paid attention.

  2. The signal

    L&D sees change first

    L&D sees the business change before anyone else: the request that keeps coming back, the skill no one trained for, the region that always runs late. Most of those signals are lost in email and spreadsheets.

    [completar com a história real da ReFrame: quando e por que a empresa começou, o problema que o time viveu, o que aprendeu operando T&D para clientes]
  3. The platform

    One place for the whole operation

    Saros is one place where a request becomes a project, a project becomes content and content becomes learning that reaches people.

History, read well, becomes a pattern

Every step leaves a record. Every record becomes history.

  1. Requestarrives with a KPI
  2. Projectmoves through the pipeline
  3. Contentis produced and approved
  4. Learningreaches people
  5. Recordevery step is kept
  6. Historyrecords add up
  7. Patternyou see what is coming

Free resources for L&D operations

Tools you can use today, whether or not you ever use Saros. Score your operation, put a number on coordination, standardize intake and read what we are learning about how L&D works.

L&D operations resources to assess your team

L&D Operating Health Check. About 7 minutes, 30 questions about how work really moves through your L&D function. You get a Health Score, one of 8 operating profiles, scores on 5 dimensions from demand to impact, and the hours your team loses to coordination. No email needed to see your score.

Start the Health Check →
Calculate what coordination costs

Coordination cost calculator. Enter your team size, the share of time spent on coordination and an hourly cost. In about a minute you get the yearly cost in hours and dollars, and a one-page report you can send to your CFO.

Calculate your coordination cost →
Templates

Training request intake form. The 9 questions every training request should answer, a triage checklist and a prioritization scorecard. Fill it in online with live scoring, or download the PDF.

Get the free intake form template →
Research

State of Learning Operations 2027. An annual report built from anonymized Health Check data: how L&D teams take in requests, prioritize, produce and prove impact. Planned for May 2027. [página fica com noindex até o relatório sair]
